- Cleaner's POV: practical, observant, maybe a bit wry. They notice things others don't.
- Mystery hook: something found — a ticket, a note, a suitcase, a photograph, a key. Or a person who doesn't belong. Maybe a woman who seems to be waiting for someone, or a man who's been waiting for hours.
- Keep it an opening scene — so it should end with a hook, not resolve.

Length: A scene, maybe 600-900 words. Format: prose, no headers needed. Maybe a title? Could include a title like "First Light" or just dive in. I'll write it as prose with a title perhaps. Title: "First Light" or "The 5:40" or "Cleaning the Station" — maybe "Dawn Shift" or "The Cleaner." I'll go with "First Light."

Opening lines:

"The station at dawn was a different building than the one I cleaned at night."

The station at dawn was a different building than the one I cleaned at night. At night it was all noise and light — announcements, the clatter of luggage, the smell of coffee and cigarettes. At dawn it was quiet, and the quiet was the part I liked, because the quiet was when I could see what the station was doing.

I arrived at 5:30, when the last train had gone and the first one hadn't come yet. The lights were still on, but the fluorescents had that buzz that meant the building was half-asleep. I swept the ticket hall. I mopped the floor. I emptied the trash cans. I did all of this slowly, because the station was mine for a few hours, and I liked to know it.

Then I noticed the man.

He was sitting on the bench by the departures board, near the stairs, and he was asleep — or he was pretending to be asleep. His head was tipped to one side, and his eyes were open, and he was watching the board. The board said 5:40, and then 6:15, and then 6:50, and the man was watching the 6:15.

I didn't touch him. I didn't wake him. I just stood there and watched him, and then I did what I always did: I looked at what he was holding.

He was holding a ticket. It was a paper ticket, the kind that had been printed before the machines took over, and it was for the 6:15. The 6:15 was the train that left at 6:15, and the man was waiting for it, and the ticket was for the 6:15, and the man was waiting for it.
